comments.text: I really feel like Dr Mike is undervaluing the cosmetic portion of these procedures.  Several years ago I traveled down to Panama to assist with charity children's eye surgeries. I basically just transported people around, the Drs and Techs were incredible working 14 hours with no break time between patients (literally it was set up with room for 2 operating tables in each room and we would roll in a new patient before they even finished the previous one).  The majority of things that were fixed were conditions like a child being cross-eyed.  While that may not seem vital at first, the cultures from may of the small villages would completely ostracize people with a physical abnormality.  Even if the person could function just fine, they were going to be complete outcasts with no hope and jobs, spouses, access to education, etc.  The unfortunate reality is that this type of estrangement is very common particularly in your poorer, less developed parts of the world.

comments.text:
The issue I take with people who hate videos (of consenting) people being helped is that they essentially believe the only valid help is one done behind closed doors.

There is a long list of benefits to videoing, but even assuming absolute selfishness on Jimmy's part (which I don't believe is the case, but I might be wrong), there is still a net good. So what is he makes millions from it, those (consenting) people received care. They had something done for them that they were struggling to obtain.

I hope people are videoing to build more money to do more good, but even if they only do it for "clout" and self-enrichment, they've done a little good along the way. There are thousands of social media influences who have not done anything, yet people go after those who do with the minor issues.

I truly believe that it is easier for influencers not to do good in the community because of the critics that come out when you do. Every channel I know that has tried to help people has had controversies or at least a huge number of deeply critical comments on their videos from self-professed experts.

When someone like Jimmy spends literal millions helping people and can then create content to generate more millions from ad revenue/sponsorship to start the cycle again, he is doing more than almost all those commenters will do in a lifetime.

Do I think Jimmy or other influencers are perfect, hell no. Not remotely. Do I respect them for at least stepping out into the open where people are waiting to tear them down. Yeah, they know there are easier ways to get rich, but they decided it was still worth taking on the critics.
comments.author: @TimeWasterPB

comments.text:
Obviously, it's a good thing that people are getting life-improving procedures they otherwise wouldn't have access to; people aren't disputing that. The problem is it being turned into "content" and made into a spectacle. It's hard for me to consider that "philanthropy" when you're profiting from it. On top of that, all these good deeds sound especially hollow when you know how contestants on both editions of Beast Games were treated, with them for some reason having their personal belonging (including medication) withheld and access to basic needs like water, food, beds and hygiene items denied (including menstruation products), with the show frequently highlighting how miserable their home lives are and how desperately they need the money. You know, the kind of money Mr Beast happily throws around in most videos, but in this case it's more fun to dangle above poor people's heads, I guess. Oh and speaking of money, they also apparently didn't pay at least some of the contestants the overtime pay they were owed, among many other issues.

Mr Beast may well be genuine about his desire to help people, but his history makes it clear that he views paying for 1000 people's healthcare and crushing the hopes and dreams of 1000 people while forcing them to live in inhumane conditions that may genuinely threaten their health and life as equally valid video material.

I also really don't think charities making videos is a valid comparison. They make videos to show what they do, the results they get and the importance of their work, not to make sensationalised content that focuses mostly on how generous the billionaire is being on a channel that also has zero problem showing a man on the brink of going stir crazy from isolation weep profusely because he just learned that the one person he's seen regularly in months, and has gone closely attached to, just died, before moving on with the rest of the challenge as if nothing had happened because to Mr Beast, the death of a man and the emotional devastation of another are virtually nothing.

And I mean, if one person has the money to finance this many procedures without issue, while thousands have to live with disabilities or die unnecessarily, maybe that goes to show we should tax billionaires more, instead of having the Poors pray to be blessed with being made into a YouTube video. Maybe, if we want to change this unfair system, we need to stop normalising the exploitation of the masses for the benefit of the already wealthy.

comments.text: This video made me think about just how important early screening and intervention is. My brother was born with congenital aortic coarctation. His doctor knew he had a grade 5 murmur but just kept waiting to see if he would "grow out of it" until my mom put her foot down and they got a referral to Nationwide Children's Hospital here in Columbus. He had agonizing pain in his legs for years but his doctor just kept telling us it was "growing pains" even though he was screaming and crying when the pain was severe. Children's Hospital was excellent with their care and diagnosed him in just one visit after a series of scans. His defect was repaired with a relatively simple cath procedure, which he just had redone when he turned 18. The hospital will also continue seeing him for the rest of his life if he desires. Sometimes I wonder what would've happened if we didn't get that referral because the blockage was very severe. I feel like he kind of suffered for nothing because it was so easy to fix and other than blood pressure medication and a yearly cardiology visit he doesn't need any special care. That level of care would be so easy to implement in areas outside of the US with adequate funding and staffing. Glad to see Mr. Beast has an interest in making that happen, no matter how corny his thumbnails are.
